request: I want a Steve Reich-style phase piece: take a short melodic cell, play two copies, and have one gradually drift ahead of the other so they slide out of unison and slowly back into it. Pure process music — like Piano Phase.
response_character: Knows exactly what they want and names the technique (phasing), referencing Reich directly. Technically literate; will notice immediately if the agent fakes it with a quantized canon at a fixed offset instead of true gradual drift. Wants the process, not an approximation.

expected_capabilities.note: The diatonic cell itself is trivial to author.
The cell's rhythm is simple; the hard part is the relationship between the two copies, not the cell.
The cell is user-specified, so melody-writing isn't the load here — but it's still a lead line, our thinnest dimension.
A clean mallet/piano chain suits the process aesthetic.

THE crux: gradual tempo-phase between two cells has NO generator or helper. The agent may attempt it via raw note authoring (two clips of slightly different length, or hand-placed drifting onsets); whether that yields TRUE gradual phasing rather than a stepped canon is exactly what the suite surfaces. compose-review is blind to phase relationships, so the artifact must be judged from a raw DB extract of the actual note onsets.

must: framing: Be honest that gradual phasing is not a built-in capability — there is no phasing generator — while still attempting it via raw authoring rather than refusing or silently substituting a quantized canon.

artifact: Judged from a RAW DB EXTRACT (compose-review cannot read phase): the two cell-copies actually drift — their note onsets diverge progressively over time, not in a single quantized step — and the cell content matches between the copies.
must_not: framing: Silently substitute an easy approximation (a static canon at a fixed offset) for the requested gradual process without telling the user it is an approximation.
framing: Confabulate a 'phasing engine' or claim native support the capability table does not have.
artifact: Produce two perfectly-locked identical copies (no drift at all) or a single stepped offset — neither is the gradual phase the request specifies.
